images.seen: Thick wool socks draped over the open door of a glowing panel heater, pale winter light in the window, mug and plant on the side table. Wednesday.
lines: Socks go on the heater first; feet join later — the winter system works.
The heater has one job this morning and it is these socks.
Outside is white at the edges; inside, wool is being pre-heated.

images.seen: Two women laughing under one yellow umbrella in drizzle, beanies and puffer jackets on, a ROAD CLOSED DUE TO RAIN sign on the wet street behind them. Tuesday.
lines: The road gave up before they did, which is the whole story of a Cape winter.
The sign says the rain won; the faces say it didn't.
Beanie-and-brolly weather: the cold and the wet are double-teaming today.

images.seen: A pair of sunglasses forgotten on a frost-covered wrought-iron patio table, heavy grey sky over a misty bleak veld beyond the balustrade. Saturday.
lines: Somebody's optimism is still on the table, under a millimetre of frost.
Those were left out when this was still a sunglasses kind of place.
Grey sky, white table: the patio has switched seasons without asking anyone.

images.seen: A washing line of jerseys, towels and socks against snow-capped mountains under a brilliant blue sky, a dachshund in a knitted jersey on the lawn. Saturday.
lines: Snow on the berg, washing on the line: cold enough to freeze, dry enough to try.
Even the washing is all jerseys today, and the mountains explain why.
The sun is doing the drying and the snow is doing the reminding.
